summary.lessons_learned: Boundary semantics matter: with hitstunTimer = N*DT, ai() resumes on step N+1, not N — test asserts this explicitly. The bck/ test dir contains archived bit-roted tests (bad import paths) that fail standalone but are excluded from run-all.mjs; don't treat those as regressions.

2.2.name: Vertical pop on hard hits (2D knockback)

summary.lessons_learned: The core 2D impulse already worked (knockback.test.js proves an upward normal lofts), but our specific attack normals carry no y component at ground level — verifying against the real dirMode math, not just the generic mechanism, was the crux. Pop must be applied after the impulse and divided by resist so mass resists the loft too; it must NOT fire on the no-op path (Thorn) — the early return guard keeps that intact.
summary.tradeoffs: Pop is a separate fixed knob rather than blending vertical into the push normal: cleaner tuning (vertical feel independent of horizontal direction) but one more field on the setting. Pop scales with knockbackResist like the shove — heavier enemies get a proportionally smaller loft, consistent with §3.
summary.done: Added an optional 'pop' field (fixed upward launch, px/s) to the knockback setting: applyKnockback() now adds victim.vy -= pop/resist on top of the directional impulse, so hard hits loft victims off the ground and they fall back under existing gravity (§5). Set pop values on the three committed attacks in heroDefs.js: supermove 150 (visible ~1-2 body-height loft at GRAVITY 1500), cartwheel 50, sweep 40 — ordered super > special melee, nothing exaggerated. Added acceptance tests to attackKnockback.test.js: supermove hit with a horizontal dash normal sets vy upward proportional to strength (exact -pop check + mass-resistance scaling + sweep-hops-smaller-than-super ordering); Thorn/no-knockback hit leaves vx/vy/hitstunTimer untouched.
summary.decisions: Chose option (b) from the task context: an explicit per-attack 'pop' field consumed by applyKnockback, instead of biasing the caller-derived normal. The alongVelocity/fromAttacker normals for these ground-level attacks are effectively horizontal (hero vy=0 during dash, same-height center-to-center), so the existing 2D mechanism alone would impart no upward motion — the pop guarantees the §5 loft regardless of geometry. Values left as v1 starting points for final tuning in 2.3.

3.1.name: Merge contact/bossContact into velocity-scaled body knockback

summary.tradeoffs: The hero has two redundant timer mechanisms (plain fields + unified timers) bridged by a small transfer block in the contact handler. This is intentional: it keeps takeHit() unchanged for projectile/explosion sources while letting body-contact use the unified applyKnockback math. A future task could unify all hero damage through applyKnockback if desired.
summary.decisions: Used the compatibility-shim approach: applyKnockback writes plain fields on the hero, and the contact handler immediately transfers them to the hero's Timers system. This preserves the existing intangible flag + render blink mechanism without modifying takeHit() or the timer system. Bosses get their harder hit from a larger base (340 vs 260) plus the motion term picking up their actual velocity — no separate category needed. Kept KNOCKBACK_PROFILES contact/bossContact rows since they're still referenced by tests and DEFAULT_KNOCKBACK_SOURCE.
summary.lessons_learned: applyKnockback normalizes internally via the caller-provided normal vector, so the caller must pass an already-normalized direction. The old takeHit normalized dirX/dirY internally. Both produce identical results when the input magnitudes match. The motion term uses dot(attacker_velocity, normal) clamped to >=0, so only forward momentum amplifies the hit — a receding enemy can't add force.
summary.done: Replaced the layer-based boss/regular contact branch with applyKnockback using a bodyKnockback setting carried on each Enemy. Enemy constructor now assigns bodyKnockback (base 260 for regular, 340 for bosses; scaleBySpeed 1.0, matching old profile recovery/iFrames). The contact handler in update.js computes a normalized push normal, calls applyKnockback(hero, source, source.bodyKnockback, normal), then routes the plain hitstunTimer/iFrameTimer fields into the hero's unified timer system. Hero gained transient hitstunTimer/iFrameTimer fields (always zeroed post-transfer) as the shim between applyKnockback's plain-field writes and the hero's Timers-based state.

summary.tradeoffs: Jester gets a documentation-only note rather than a whip hitbox knockback block, because the implementation has no per-enemy-attack knockback data — enemy→hero shoves use source-keyed profiles on the hero side. Documenting 'no knockback' explicitly prevents designers from adding a fake field later.
summary.decisions: Used snake_case keys (body_knockback, scale_by_speed, dir_mode, i_frames) per task context, while keeping the JS camelCase names visible in comments so the mapping is unambiguous. Kept the boss body_knockback override as an inline comment rather than a second block, since it's a single fallback expression in enemy.js, not a separate def field. Named the hero block supermove_knockback (matching ATTACK_SUPERMOVE) rather than super_knockback from the snippet, to align with the codebase identifier.
summary.done: Added knockback blocks to the three entity YAML files, verified field-for-field against the implementation (js/knockback.js typedef + js/heroDefs.js values + js/enemy.js bodyKnockback defaults). enemy.yaml: body_knockback block with base/scale_by_speed/hitstun/i_frames plus boss-override note. hero.yaml: sweep_knockback, cartwheel_knockback, supermove_knockback blocks matching heroDefs.js exactly, with a field legend and a comment noting explosion knockback is carried on the explosion subject (knockback.md §7). jester.yaml: explicit note that the whip carries NO knockback setting (enemy attacks shove the hero via source-keyed KNOCKBACK_PROFILES in hero.js; v1 scope is hero→enemy only). All three files parse as valid YAML.
summary.lessons_learned: The plan snippet's enemy example (base: 60, dir_mode: from_attacker) did not match the implemented values (base: 260 regular / 340 boss, no dirMode field on body contact) — always verify against the actual implementation before writing doc YAML. Also the snippet omitted the pop field entirely; the implemented KnockbackSetting includes pop for all three hero attacks.

3.4.name: Preserve existing enemy-to-hero knockback through the refactor

summary.lessons_learned: The contact path's expected vx/vy differ from the simple dirX=1,dirY=0 reference because the handler bakes a -0.6 upward component into the normal before normalization (len=√1.36≈1.166), giving vx≈222.9 not 260 — the regression must use the handler's actual input, not the profile strength directly.
summary.decisions: Pinned expected values as an explicit REF table mirroring knockback-reference.txt instead of deriving them from KNOCKBACK_PROFILES/enemy defaults at runtime, so the test fails if EITHER side drifts from the captured pre-refactor reference. Used real Hero + Enemy instances (not stand-ins) to exercise the actual code paths including the default bodyKnockback fallback logic.
summary.tradeoffs: Test replicates the contact handler's normal construction and timer transfer inline rather than importing update.js (which has heavy DOM/game-state deps), so a future change to those two snippets in update.js would need the test updated too — acceptable for a regression pin.
summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/test/knockbackRegression.test.js (9 tests, all passing) proving the enemy→hero knockback refactor is behavior-preserving: body contact via applyKnockback+enemy.bodyKnockback reproduces the pre-refactor contact/bossContact vectors (260/340 along the (±1,-0.6) normalized normal → vx≈222.9/vy≈-133.8, rec 0.25/0.30, iFrames 0.60/0.70); projectile/heavyProj/explosion via takeHit reproduce their exact reference values (220/300/380, matching rec + intangible windows). Also covers radial explosion direction scaling and i-frame absorption on both paths.
